title: The published Week 10 board originates a line for a game that has already been played
finding: research/nfl/results.json originates 14 Week 10 games, including WAS @ NYG. That game finished on 2026-11-12 with Washington 24, New York Giants 21, and its own official game page prints FINAL.
detail: The frozen fixture file was captured on 2026-11-12, before the Thursday game. This desk originates 13 games and excludes the one already played.
recommended: Re-read the Week 10 schedule page after Monday 2026-11-16 and regenerate the board, or mark any settled fixture on the board as settled rather than originated.

title: Two desks publish different directional records for the same season
finding: This desk records 70-50 (0.5833) for the board's own side. nfl-results/analysis.json records 82-51 (0.6165).
detail: A sensitivity run rules out the most likely cause. Forcing this desk's home allowance to the 2.0 points the other desk assumes gives 62-58 (0.5167), which is further away, not closer. The difference is in the functional form and the shrinkage.
recommended: Grade both models on one frozen forecast table and publish the difference. Suggestion SG-04.

title: The older board's two key parameters are assumptions, not NFL figures
finding: nfl_origination uses a home allowance of 2.0 points and a margin standard deviation of 13.86, and discloses both as project assumptions. Measured from 137 official final scores they are -0.0219 (n = 137) and 13.2251 (n = 137).
detail: The home allowance carries a 95% interval of [-2.2365, 2.1927], which contains both zero and the conventional two points. This season does not separate them.
recommended: Keep the measured value and publish the interval. Do not silently switch the older board.

title: Most injury rows carry no game status, so any replacement count is a floor
finding: 301 of 326 Week 10 injury rows print no game status at all.
detail: A replacement is only implied where the league states an absence. The report states one on 25 rows, so the depth table counts what is published rather than what a reader might assume.
recommended: Suggestion SG-03: find the field on another page, or publish the ceiling as the finding.

title: Houston's depth chart cannot be read
finding: The Houston club site renders a heading and an image with no table. The failure was reproduced on two independent reads by two different sessions.
detail: Houston therefore has no printed ranks and no replacement depth. The cell is blank, not estimated.
recommended: Try the club roster page, or accept the blank and keep it flagged.

title: Captured depth charts are undated or stale
finding: Chicago prints a chart date of 10/31/2026, which precedes the injury ledger it is joined to. Denver, Philadelphia and Tampa print no date. Philadelphia's chart is self-labelled unofficial.
detail: A replacement depth is only as current as the chart it comes from. 30 of 31 captured charts carry no printed date.

title: The Rams are printed two different ways, which silently breaks a join
finding: NFL.com prints the Rams as LA. The standings capture in nfl-skill-cfdd uses LAR. Joining the two without normalising reports the club as missing: this session's first reconciliation failed with exactly that symptom.
detail: After normalising LA to LAR the reconciliation is exact: 192 of 192 club fields match and 6,291 points are scored each way.
recommended: Normalise at load and record the printed code beside the canonical one, which is what this desk now does.

title: Sixteen standings display fields are withheld
finding: The rendered standings table prints three unnamed three-part records and two unnamed decimals. The page does not say which is home, road, division or conference.
detail: Withheld rather than guessed. Correct handling, retained here.

title: The README count of official scores is now one short
finding: README.md states 136 official scores. The feed now holds 137 after the Week 10 Thursday game was added.
detail: The count was right when it was written. It is a staleness, not an error.
recommended: Update to 137 with the game's source link.

title: The frozen standings snapshot is superseded for two clubs
finding: Washington is frozen at 2-5-1 with PF 172, and New York Giants at 5-2-1 with PF 182. The standings page read today shows Washington 3-5-1 with PF 196 and the Giants 5-3-1 with PF 203.
detail: Correct for a frozen snapshot, and it is the root cause of RF-01. Nothing was back-filled into the frozen file.
recommended: Note the snapshot date prominently wherever a frozen figure is displayed.

title: No price exists anywhere in the project, and this is verified rather than assumed
finding: nfl.com returns HTTP 404 at /odds/ with no odds table, no price, no operator and no market list. A repository-wide search for committed market, price, closing, CLV, ROI or stake values returns nothing numeric.
detail: This is the single largest constraint on the project. It is why the difference column, the staking table and every reward are blank.

title: Two statistical defects found in this session's own code and fixed before publication
finding: The Benjamini-Hochberg step-up was computed from the smallest p-value forwards, which drags every later value down to the smallest one and reported an adjusted p of 0 for a raw p of 1. Separately, the t-test for a Pearson correlation returned values greater than 1.
detail: Both were visible in the output rather than in the code: every adjusted p printed as 0.0000, and two p-values printed as 1.94 and 1.74. Fixed by running the step-up from the largest rank downwards and by using the identity P(|T| > t) = I_x(df/2, 1/2) with x = df/(df + t^2). Both are now checked against known values: the incomplete beta returns 0.5 at (1, 1, 0.5), the normal CDF returns 0.975 at 1.96, and a correlation of exactly zero returns p = 1.
recommended: None. Recorded so the fix is not mistaken for a silent edit.

title: Three leaderboard defects found in this session's own code and fixed
finding: The ranking score divided by the strength of evidence instead of multiplying by it, so a result with p = 0.90 ranked first. Control entries were being promoted to Provisional. Blocked entries showed performance gates as failures when those gates do not apply.
detail: The score is now log10(n) x distance from the reference x -log10(p); controls carry a Control tier and are never ranked; and a blocked strategy marks the performance gates not applicable rather than failed.
recommended: None. Recorded for the same reason as RF-12.

title: The totals board scores 50.4%, and that is the expected result
finding: Grading a forecast against its own number must produce a coin flip. It does: 61 overs and 60 unders on 121 games.
detail: Published as a control so the number is not misread as a result. The totals model's real score is its skill against the league mean, which is -0.1040 - worse than the reference.

title: The player-props division has no graded entries at all
finding: 2 entries are blocked because no per-game player log was retrieved from any official source.
detail: The division exists, its rules are written, and every column in it is blank. Publishing a dependence for a prop without the underlying numbers would be a fabrication.
